options.content:
# Ignite
Use this dashboard to monitor the Ignite data-grid service in this deployment. It provides visibility into cluster activity, memory and cache behavior, and operational health signals. Compare the affected node or cache with overall cluster trends to distinguish a localized resource issue from a broader cluster condition.

panels.description: Turn on debug logs on ignite to get details or tail the audit-log Kafka topic
panels.title: Discovery / Continuity Error Counters

panels.description: Metric records dropped for tenant/objectType with the reason for the drop
panels.title: Dropped record counts

panels.description: Error rate during normalization. Turn on debug logs on ignite to get details
panels.title: Normalization errors

options.content: Ignite registers cluster membership/leadership in ZooKeeper with an ephemeral node. An ordinary **disconnect** is survivable, but a confirmed **session expiration** permanently invalidates that registration - and a new authenticated session does NOT recreate it. Until the process restarts, membership/election is broken: this is exactly what makes the retention controller report no leader, so **`ownership_verified` drops to 0 and the reconcile age goes stale** in the section above (existing Kafka caps stay enforced meanwhile). `ZK_EXIT_ON_SESSION_EXPIRED` (Helm default **true**, standalone default **false**) makes every member exit(1) on expiry so a supervisor (`restartPolicy: Always`) rebuilds registration via normal startup. Show **every Ignite instance** here (followers lose registration too), not just the retention owner. Warnings before expiry are best-effort. Confirm recovery via retention ownership=1 + a fresh reconcile, not ZK authentication alone; correlate with container-restart metrics and the `ZooKeeper session expired: ... exiting` log.

panels.description: Instances whose ZooKeeper session was confirmed EXPIRED and remain latched until process restart - registration/leadership is broken for these even if they re-authenticated. GOOD: 0 (green). BAD: >=1 (red) = those instances need a restart (automatic if the exit policy is on). This is the primary ZK incident signal.
panels.title: Sessions expired (latched)

panels.description: Live instances currently reporting no ZooKeeper session (scraped but connected=0). GOOD: 0. WATCH: >=1 (yellow) = an active disconnect episode; a brief blip is usually fine, a sustained one risks expiration. Instances that are down/unscraped are not counted here - use the up/target alerts for those.
panels.title: Disconnected now

panels.description: Whether the fail-fast policy is enabled (`ZK_EXIT_ON_SESSION_EXPIRED`). ENABLED (green) = members exit on expiry and a supervisor rebuilds registration automatically. DISABLED (yellow) = expired instances will NOT self-heal; you must restart them manually (standalone default). Shows the minimum across instances, so mixed settings read as DISABLED - keep the policy consistent cluster-wide.
panels.title: Exit-on-expire policy

panels.description: Count of fail-fast process exits triggered by session expiration in the last hour (summed across instances). Informational: nonzero means the self-heal path fired and pods restarted. The final increment before exit can be lost/unscraped, so corroborate with container-restart metrics and logs; counters also reset on restart.
panels.title: Expiration exits (1h)

panels.description: Per-instance authentication state over time (1=has session). GREEN = connected, RED = no session. Each row is one Ignite instance - followers matter too. Brief red blips are survivable disconnects; a red band ending without recovery often precedes/accompanies expiration (see the expired timeline). Missing = Unknown, not Connected.
panels.title: ZooKeeper session connected (per instance)

panels.description: How long each currently-disconnected instance has been without a session (0 when connected). GOOD: flat 0. BAD: a rising line = a sustained disconnect that risks expiration as it approaches the negotiated session timeout. Observed disconnection is not an exact estimate of server-side expiry time.
panels.title: Current disconnection duration (per instance)

panels.description: Rate of ZooKeeper session transitions across all instances. disconnected = unavailability episodes after a prior session; reconnected = re-authentication (incl. a new post-expiry session); expired = confirmed expirations (the serious one). Repeated events within one episode are not double-counted. Use this for episode history; brief blips whose gauges were never scraped can still appear here.
panels.title: Session events (disconnect / reconnect / expire)

panels.description: Per-instance latched expiration flag over time (1 after confirmed expiry, until process restart). GREEN = OK, RED = expired and NOT self-recovered. A red band means that instance's membership/leadership stayed broken for that whole period - correlate the band's end with a container restart. In exit-policy-off deployments this is the key persistent-risk signal.
panels.title: Session expired / latched (per instance)

panels.description: Correlation aid, NOT emitted by this feature: container restarts per Ignite pod over 1h from kube-state-metrics. Expect this to rise shortly after expiration exits when the fail-fast policy is on. May show No data if kube-state-metrics is absent or the pod name match below does not fit your deployment - adjust the `pod` matcher to your naming. Process exit counters can lose their final increment, so this external signal is the more reliable restart audit.
panels.title: Ignite container restarts (external · kube-state-metrics)
